name: bounce2d
description: Landing on things and being thrown back: a Bouncer that falls onto a Bouncy surface from above leaves it with an upward speed, as a jumper does on platforms, springs and trampolines. Surfaces are one-way (the Bouncer passes through them going up and from the side) and can be single-use, break instead of bouncing, or be destroyed by the landing (a monster stomped on). The y axis points down, as on screen.

components.name: Bouncer
components.description: The entity lands on Bouncy surfaces. It needs a Position, a Velocity and a Collider (its box is what lands). The tick it lands, its bottom edge is compared with where it was one tick before, so a fast fall cannot go through a thin surface. bounces counts the bounces so far.

components.name: Bouncy
components.description: A surface that throws a landing Bouncer up at strength units per second (a Collider gives its size; only its top edge counts). A Bouncer that falls onto it from above lands; one that rises through it, or that passes beside it, does not. vanish removes the surface after one bounce. breaks makes it give way instead of throwing the Bouncer back: the Bouncer keeps falling, and the surface stops being Bouncy and drops at fall_speed. kills removes the surface after the bounce too, for a monster that is jumped on.

systems.name: bounce
systems.description: For every falling Bouncer, finds the highest Bouncy surface whose top edge its bottom edge crossed this tick, with the two overlapping sideways, and applies the landing: the Bouncer's Velocity becomes upward and it is put on the surface, unless the surface breaks. Runs after the movement and before collision2d.detect, so a monster that is jumped on is gone before anything counts what touches the player.
